# Locale entries give the operation, input tag and observed result.
# Collation entries give the fixture, line of the second string and observed
# relation (previous vs. current). All listed cases run.

# rbbitst.txt entries give the opening <data> line and the exact changes
# from its expected UTF-16 break offsets (+extra, -missing).

# POSIX English word breaks around punctuation. Intl.Segmenter has no
# relevant Unicode extension keys, so en-US-u-va-posix resolves to en-US.
rbbitst.txt 1584 -23,-24,-36,-37

# Ekuma uses a web-compatible space before AM/PM.
format.txt 35 "8/8/07, 6:54 PM"
format.txt 100 "11:59:00 PM GMT"
format.txt 107 "5:00:00 PM GMT"

# The Hebrew date also differs in its zone name. In Gregorian year 99458,
# ICU4C uses GMT-08:00 because its default metazone mapping ends in 9999.
# Ekuma uses CLDR's open-ended America_Pacific mapping for Los Angeles.
format.txt 552 "Friday, 3 Heshvan 103217 at 12:00:00 AM Pacific Standard Time"

# The fixture expects other for Serbian 2E0. Ekuma and ICU4C 79.1 both
# select few. ICU4C's NumberFormatDataDrivenTest inherits isSelectPass,
# which accepts the row without comparing the plural category.
numberformattestspecification.txt 1042 few

# The German fixture lists a tenth field for Uhr at UTF-16 offsets [32, 35).
# ICU4C 79.1 returns nine fields ending at 31, leaving " Uhr" as a shared
# literal. Its checkMixedFormattedValue helper checks only returned fields,
# so the extra expected field goes unchecked.
cdateintervalformattest.c/formatRangeToParts 396 "shared day 27\nshared literal . \nshared month September\nshared literal  \nshared year 2010\nshared literal , \nstartRange hour 15\nstartRange literal :\nstartRange minute 00\nshared literal –\nendRange hour 22\nendRange literal :\nendRange minute 00\nshared literal  Uhr"
